No. Hansen/UMD mapped tree-cover loss of about 81.3 ha in 2021, which is roughly 2.2% of the 3,643.5 ha property. The evidence supports this loss, since later years were observed and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the affected area.

Most of the loss was in planted forest (68.1 ha, Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). The rest was outside mapped forest (13.2 ha), and none was in native forest. Another 37.3 ha of loss came in patches under 0.5 ha, which are not counted as an event.

This evidence cannot show that deforestation or land-use change occurred, because Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as cutting a plantation. It also cannot show the cause, whether the change was legal, who was responsible, or any compliance finding.
